newsitem.title: CANADA: Anvil Range reaches labor deal at Faro.
newsitem.headline: Anvil Range reaches labor deal at Faro.

text.p: Anvil Range Mining Corp said on Wednesday that it has reached an agreement with the union representing workers at the Faro lead and zinc operation in Canada's Yukon.
About 350 of 420 employees at the site are unionized, but about 300 of those have been laid off since the mine was temporarily shut down last December. The mill has continued to operate.
Anvil Range chief financial officer Victor Wells said the three-year agreement retroactive to November 1, 1996 was ratified by workers.
"There were (wage) increases over the three-year period in all the job classifications. We're pleased to have labor peace," Wells said in a telephone interview.
The Faro mill, which produces about 12,500 tonnes of ore daily, is on schedule to close at the end of March.
Wells said the company is still working on obtaining new financing to start a stripping program. "We're optimistic about re-opening. We've been helped a lot by better metal prices," he said.
